0.note: The word translated as **chief musician** likely refers to the person in charge of music for worship. Some languages may have a term for a music leader. Alternate translation: [For the music director] or [For the leader of worship music]

**Jeduthun** was a Levite who was one of the worship leaders in the temple during the reign of David. The expression **on Jeduthun** could mean: (1) that David gave this song to Jeduthun and his choir to perform. Alternate translation: [for Jeduthun’s choir] or (2) that singers were to perform this song in the style of Jeduthun’s choir. Alternate translation: [perform in the style of Jeduthun]

1.note: The phrase **I said** is here represented as introducing a direct quotation although it was likely an unspoken thought. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing unspoken thoughts in your language as modeled in the UST. It may not be necessary to represent this phrase explicitly.

This is an imperative, but it communicates David’s personal resolve rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a personal resolve for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a personal resolve. Alternate translation: [I resolve to guard my ways]

David is speaking of his behavior as if it were paths or **ways** where there could be a **guard** posted to control access. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [control my conduct]
David is using the term **tongue** to mean speaking. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from sinning by what I say]

David is speaking of restraining his speech as if he were putting a **muzzle** on his **mouth** like one would muzzle an animal. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will keep silent]

2.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **silence**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [by not saying a word]

David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [I refrained from saying anything good]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **pain**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and my suffering increased]

The expression **was stirred up** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and my silence only made my pain worse]

David uses the word **and** here to indicate a contrast rather than adding information. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [but instead, my pain]

3.note: David is speaking of his intense emotions as if his **heart became hot** like something burning with fire. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I burned with anxiety within me]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **sighing**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the more I was distressed]

David is speaking of his emotional turmoil as if **fire burned** within him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my distress intensified]

The phrase **I spoke with my tongue** introduces a direct quotation that begins in the next verse. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. Alternate translation: [I finally said,]
David is using the term **tongue** to mean speaking. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I spoke these words]

4.note: This is an imperative, but it communicates a polite request rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please let me know my end, Yahweh]

David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [when my life will end]

5.note: David is speaking of his life span as if it were **days** that could be measured out in **handbreadths** of time, a very small measure. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you have made my lifetime as short as a handbreadth]

David says **my lifetime is as nothing before you** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [and my lifetime is extremely brief from your point of view]

The point of this comparison is that just as the time that a man **stands** or lives is frail and transient, so is **vapor** or a mere breath. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [each man’s life is frail and transient]

6.note: The point of this comparison is that just as an **image** is insubstantial and fleeting, so is a person’s life. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [a man walks about but has no real substance]

Here David is speaking of people going through life as if it were **a man** who **walks about**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [people go through life]

David is not referring to a specific **man**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [a person]

David is speaking of people’s pursuits as if they were **vapor**, something futile and insubstantial. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [surely they make an uproar over what is futile and worthless]
The pronoun **they** refers to people in general. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [everyone bustles around]

David assumes that readers will know that by **heaps up** he means acquiring a lot of possessions. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [He acquires possessions]
The pronoun **them** refers to the things that the person has heaped up. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [who will be getting all of those things]

7.note: The word **And** here introduces a transition from David’s reflection on the brevity of life to his direct appeal to God. If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [Now then]

David is using the question form to emphasize that there is nothing worth waiting for apart from God. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [there is nothing I should wait for, Lord!]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **hope**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [What I wait hopefully for]

8.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **transgressions**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from all the ways I have sinned against you]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **reproach**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [someone whom a fool insults]

9.q: נֶ֭אֱלַמְתִּי לֹ֣א אֶפְתַּח־פִּ֑⁠י כִּ֖י אַתָּ֣ה עָשִֽׂיתָ
9.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Because you have done it, I am mute; I do not open my mouth]

The expression **I do not open my mouth** represents David choosing not to speak. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I do not say anything]

David is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb translated as **you have done** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that it is Yahweh who is responsible for what has happened. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [because of what you specifically have done]

10.note: This is an imperative, but it communicates a polite request rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please remove your plague from upon me]

David is using **your hand** as part of a common expression of his culture as seen in Psalm 32:4, “your hand was heavy upon me” to mean that Yahweh has afflicted or disciplined him severely. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the way you have afflicted me]

David is stating the pronoun **I** separately, even though the verb translated as **I am finished** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize his own desperate condition. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [indeed, I am finished]

11.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **rebukes**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [By rebuking a man]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for the sinful things he has done]

David is not referring to a specific **man**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you discipline a person]

The point of this comparison is that just as a **moth** gradually destroys clothing, so Yahweh destroys what a person treasures. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and like a moth destroys clothing, you dissolve the things he desires]

David is speaking of all human existence as if it were **vapor** that quickly disappears. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the similar phrase “every man stands as all vapor” in verse 5. Alternate translation: [Surely all mankind lives but a short time]

12.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **prayer**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what I pray]
David is using the term **ear** to mean hearing. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and hear]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **deaf**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [Please pay attention]

David is speaking of his temporary time on earth as if he were a **sojourner** and a **foreigner** who is only passing through. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am only passing through with you, a temporary visitor]
David is using the term **fathers** to mean “ancestors.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my forebears]

13.note: Here, **that** marks **I may be cheerful** as the goal or purpose of David’s request for Yahweh to **Look away** from him. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [Turn your angry gaze away from me so that I may be cheerful]

David is referring to dying in a polite way by using the phrase **I go and I am no more**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [I pass away]
